say.en: How to do it — 8 steps, each with its reason
say.ur: Kaise karein — 8 qadam, har ek ki wajah ke saath

say.en: Choose and record the comparable sign. Example: right neck rotation reaches 50 degrees and pain starts at 45. Write it down so you can prove change later.
say.ur: Comparable sign choose aur record karein; misal ke taur par right neck rotation 50 degrees tak pohanchti hai aur 45 degrees par dard shuru hota hai.

say.en: Screen for red flags. Ask about night pain, unexplained weight loss, recent trauma, dizziness or neurological symptoms before touching.
say.ur: Red flags screen karein, jaise raat ka dard, baghair wazeh wajah weight kam hona, recent trauma, chakkar ya neurological symptoms.

say.en: Position for comfort. Support the joint so surrounding muscles can relax. A guarding muscle will block any glide you try.
say.ur: Joint ko comfortable position mein support karein taake aas-paas ke muscles relax kar saken.

text.en: Support the arm and stay close to the joint line.
text.ur: Support the arm and stay close to the joint line.

say.en: Place a broad, specific contact. One hand fixes the bone that should stay still. The other contacts the moving bone close to the joint line. Take up the skin slack first so you move the joint, not the skin.
say.ur: Ek hand se us bone ko stabilize karein jo still rehni chahiye aur doosray se joint line ke qareeb moving bone par specific contact banayein; pehle skin ka slack lein.

say.en: One hand supports the proximal humerus; the mobilizing hand contacts the anterior humeral head/proximal humerus broadly.
say.ur: One hand supports the proximal humerus; the mobilizing hand contacts the anterior humeral head/proximal humerus broadly.

text.en: One hand supports the proximal humerus; the mobilizing hand contacts the anterior humeral head/proximal humerus broadly.
text.ur: One hand supports the proximal humerus; the mobilizing hand contacts the anterior humeral head/proximal humerus broadly.

text.en: Stabilize the scapula/acromial region so the humeral head glide is isolated.
text.ur: Stabilize the scapula/acromial region so the humeral head glide is isolated.

say.en: Use your body weight, not your fingers. Lean smoothly through relaxed arms. Finger-only pressure makes jerky, painful oscillations.
say.ur: Sirf fingers se zor dene ke bajaye relaxed arms aur body weight se smooth movement dein.

text.en: Posterior glide of the humeral head relative to the glenoid.
text.ur: Posterior glide of the humeral head relative to the glenoid.

say.en: Start low and ask. Begin with a low grade. Local pressure is fine. Sharp pain, pins and needles or symptoms spreading down the limb mean stop.
say.ur: Low grade se shuru karein aur patient se symptoms poochhein. Tez dard, pins-and-needles ya limb mein phailti symptoms hon to rok dein.

say.en: How much? Typical teaching range: about 1-2 oscillations per second, 30-60 seconds per set, 2-4 sets. Grades I-II for pain, III-IV for stiffness. This is a starting point; the patient's response sets the real dose.
say.ur: Aam teaching range takreeban 1–2 oscillations per second, har set 30–60 seconds aur 2–4 sets hai. Dard ke liye Grades I–II aur stiffness ke liye Grades III–IV ka zikr hota hai. Yeh sirf starting range hai; asal dose patient ke response ke mutabiq hoti hai.

say.en: Treat, rest, then retest. After a set, ask the patient to repeat the comparable sign. Keep, progress or change the technique based on that answer.
say.ur: Set ke baad comparable sign dobara test karein aur response ke mutabiq technique rakhein, badlein ya progress karein.

say.en: Hand the gain back to the patient. Finish with active movement or loading in the new range, so the improvement is used rather than lost.
say.ur: Aakhir mein active movement ya loading karwayein taake patient nayi range ko khud use kare.
